results.content: Are these poll numbers in the room with us? President Donald Trump took to Truth Social on Saturday to boast about his supposedly “great” poll numbers, despite his approval rating being at rock-bottom levels. Recent polling averages from The New York Times have Trump’s overall approval rating sitting at 38%, with 59% disapproval. One of the most eye-opening polls in recent months came from CNN in late July, which showed Trump at 34% approval, matching a record low from his first term. Joe Biden at this point in his term in 2022, with inflation from the COVID-19 pandemic still high, had a 37% overall approval rating, according to the Pew Research Center. results.content: President Donald Trump’s approval rating ahead of the midterm elections sits at a lower point than other modern American presidents, according to polling data from the Pew Research Center and Quinnipiac University. Trump’s declining approval rating has driven Democratic hopes that they could retake a majority of seats in both the House of Representatives and the Senate. Trump Approval Rating Compared to Biden, Bush and Obama Quinnipiac University and the Pew Research Center have consistently tracked presidential approval ratings across recent administrations and offer key insights into how Trump’s approval stacks up against his predecessors.
